newsitem.title: Japan: TIFFE Euroyen end weaker on long-liquidation.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end weaker on long-liquidation.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures ended weaker on Wednesday as dealers who went long in the morning sold in the afternoon, traders said.

The selling in the aftenroon was partly attributed to news that a senior government official said the downside risk of the Japanese economy has decreased, giving more freedom to the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to change its monetary policy, traders said.
December moved from 98.92 to 98.97. Volume was 62,351 lots.
The government official said, however, that, "Careful study is needed before a change is made in the BOJ's monetary policy."

"The government has maintained that the economy is firm and it is unlikely to contract in the future, and the (perception) gap between the markets and the government has finally shrunk," the official said.
Some buying emerged in the morning on news that trade in Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co shares was suspended in Tokyo amid various market rumours about the bank, traders said.
One rumour held that the bank is considering equity financing worth some 100 billion yen to raise capital.
Sumitomo Trust later held a news conference and denied rumours that the bank had incurred large foreign exchange losses and that it was withdrawing from overseas operations.

Asked if Sumitomo Trust is planning to issue preferred stock, managing director Takenori Osakabe said the bank will consider every possible scheme for its fund raising, but nothing has been decided yet.
"Those who bought on the rumours started to sell in the afternoon," said a long-term credit bank dealer.
"December is unlikely to fall below 98.90 unless the market starts to factor in a rise in the BOJ's official discout rate," the dealer added.
Traders said they expected the BOJ to stop guiding key short-term interest rates before changing the discount rate, now at a record low 0.5 percent.

In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was mainly traded at 0.46 percent, down from Tuesday's 0.47. The key rate fell below 0.40 percent in the afternoon as no bank was in a hurry to raise funds ahead of the last day of the current bank reserve period on Thursday.
As expected, the BOJ kept its credit stance neutral for a third day this morning.
No new certificates of deposit (CD) were issued on Wednesday. Key three-month CDs were offer-only at 0.57 percent, unchanged from Tuesday's issued rate.
